headline: Associate @ EY-Parthenon | University of Michigan Alumni
about:
I've built my career at the intersection of technology, strategy, and innovation, shaping growth initiatives across AI, digital infrastructure, and consumer-facing technologies. With experience at firms like EY-Parthenon, Hive, and Expedia Group, I bring a unique blend of commercial diligence, operational insight, and go-to-market execution across both early-stage and enterprise environments.

As a second-year associate at EY-Parthenon, I support private equity and corporate clients through commercial due diligence, market assessments, and growth strategy projects. My focus has included data centers, data center derivatives, enterprise software, and emerging technologies, giving me exposure to both the infrastructure and application layers of the AI ecosystem.

Prior to EY-Parthenon, I gained hands-on experience with early-stage technology at Hive, supporting the go-to-market function for AI-powered collaboration tools. I also worked at Expedia Group, where I supported strategic partnerships in the travel tech space, deepening my understanding of consumer platforms and digital business models.

My work has shaped a strong interest in how AI is transforming consumer-facing industries, enabling new business models, improving user experiences, and driving operational efficiency. I'm particularly interested in the role of strategy in helping founders and investors scale companies at the forefront of this shift.

Open to connecting with others exploring the future of AI, digital infrastructure, and early-stage investing. Feel free to reach out: hallts@umich.edu

headline: Senior Director, EY-Parthenon | Energy & Capital Projects | Strategy, Digital Enablement & Delivery Modernization | Afghanistan Veteran
topSkills: Project Management • Strategic Planning • Renewable Fuels • Business Development • Financial Modeling
about:
I lead large-scale capital project and transformation programs that connect strategy, execution, and technology to drive measurable enterprise results. At EY, I lead a 95-person cross-functional team integrating operations and systems for one of the largest oil and gas mergers in recent history—harmonizing end-to-end processes and enabling more than $450 million in annual value capture.

Previously, I helped shape ExxonMobil’s corporate capital project strategy, supporting the execution of its $20–25 billion annual portfolio and advancing initiatives in low-carbon fuels, CCUS, and infrastructure development. Earlier in my career, I served as a U.S. Marine Corps officer and as a United States Navy civil engineer, responsible for leading multidisciplinary teams on major infrastructure and construction projects around the world.

I bring disciplined leadership, clarity of purpose, and a results-driven mindset to every engagement—aligning strategic vision with operational delivery. I hold an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and engineering degrees from Columbia University and Georgia Tech.

experience.description:
•	Lead a 95-person cross-functional team supporting ExxonMobil’s acquisition and integration of Pioneer Natural Resources—one of the largest energy transactions in recent history—delivering $450M+ in annual value through operational integration, business process optimization, and IT systems harmonization.

	•	Spearheaded the holistic integration of Operations business processes and supporting digital systems to ensure seamless transition and maximize synergy capture across upstream operations.

	•	Launched and lead the build-out of EY’s Capital Projects capability for the Oil & Gas sector, serving as a firmwide subject matter expert and guiding the development of next-generation offerings spanning strategy, digital enablement, and execution excellence.

	•	Partner with global account leadership to shape go-to-market initiatives, drive cross-functional collaboration, and position EY as a transformation partner for capital-intensive energy organizations.

	•	Developed and implemented strategic initiatives to optimize operations, enhance project delivery, and drive growth within the Oil/Gas/Chemicals sector.

Led the development of ExxonMobil’s renewable fuels investment portfolio within the Low Carbon Solutions and Product Solutions companies, ensuring alignment with corporate growth and decarbonization strategy.

	•	Evaluated and advanced technology investments across Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), Renewable Diesel, and waste-to-fuel pathways using thermochemical and catalytic conversion technologies.

	•	Framed integrated CO₂ utilization (CCUS) opportunities, coordinating with the Denbury acquisition team to connect biogenic and anthropogenic carbon sources with downstream project development (eFuels, methanol, MTJ, EOR, and LCAF initiatives).

	•	Developed ExxonMobil’s eFuels (Power-to-Liquids) strategy, integrating CO₂ and green hydrogen pathways to position the company for near-term market participation and long-term differentiation in synthetic fuels.

	•	Authored ExxonMobil’s Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) strategy, defining competitive positioning, regulatory compliance roadmap, and key supply-demand milestones for entry into emerging U.S. and global RNG markets.

	•	Delivered actionable investment recommendations backed by deep market assessments, technology benchmarking, and cross-functional collaboration between R&D, business development, and corporate strategy teams.

Built and led the development of ExxonMobil’s renewable fuels trading analytics platform, enhancing commercial visibility and monetization across ethanol, biodiesel, renewable diesel, and Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) markets.

	•	Designed integrated analytical tools and data models to forecast U.S. renewable fuel supply–demand balances, unifying third-party and internal data to support trading desks in Houston, London, and Singapore.

	•	Developed market correlation and valuation frameworks linking renewables with traditional energy commodities, improving hedging precision and portfolio decision-making.

	•	Enabled forward market insight and pricing strategy to support traders in contract negotiations across 130+ blending locations and optimize risk-adjusted returns.

	•	Traded Renewable Identification Number (RIN) credits (D4/D6) for ExxonMobil’s Renewable Fuel Standard compliance and hedging activities, managing $5–10M in daily positions with disciplined risk controls.

Delivered front-end engineering and execution planning for ExxonMobil’s Gas-to-Energy program — a $2B integrated onshore/offshore pipeline and GTL facility supporting national energy security and regional industrial development.

	•	Led an 8-person multidisciplinary team through site analysis, risk assessment, and execution planning under challenging environmental and logistical conditions; directed design and construction planning for 12 km of roads, 7 bridges, and a 300-acre land development supporting the GTL complex.

	•	Defined early-works execution strategy and secured JV alignment to accelerate project delivery and maintain 2025 startup milestones.

	•	Key contributor to project execution planning and FEL strategy, shaping the end-to-end delivery approach from concept selection through FEED and construction readiness.

	•	Coordinated interface alignment across engineering, contracting, and local government stakeholders to ensure schedule integrity, environmental compliance, and constructability.

Played a key role in defining the corporate and capital project strategy for ExxonMobil’s Global Projects Company, a division managing a $20–25B annual capital portfolio spanning upstream, downstream, and low-carbon developments.

	•	Partnered with senior executives to shape enterprise strategy that improved portfolio prioritization, execution readiness, and capital efficiency across global project delivery functions.

	•	Led a cross-functional assessment of construction productivity and innovation, conducting a 3-month deep-dive with 30+ ExxonMobil and EPC executives to identify improvement levers in planning, contracting, and project controls.

	•	Identified and incubated emerging technologies and delivery models to enhance cost predictability and execution performance, contributing to project cost savings of up to 10%.

	•	Established internal knowledge frameworks and implementation pathways to embed strategy outcomes into project planning standards and decision-making processes.

about:
30+ years of strategy and planning, innovation, and operating model transformation experience across state and local government agencies and multiple industry sectors.

Working with clients to design and operationalize new business models and public-private partnership ecosystems, cross-constituent experiences, operating models and organizational structures at the intersection of evolving customer needs and emerging technology possibilities. 

Transformational leader with "hands on" entrepreneurial experience developing and implementing growth strategies, disruptive product/service innovations, partner ecosystems, go-to-market (GTM) launch and scale-up strategies, and complex operating model transformations.

Specialties: Growth strategy, strategic planning and execution, discovering an organization’s purpose and developing a future-back “Strategic Roadmap” to build capability over time, design thinking at the intersection of unmet customer needs and emerging technology possibilities, business model innovation and ecosystem market mapping, customer experience journey mapping, day-in-the-life ethnography and insights synthesis, MVP offering design, experimental pilots to "de-risk" assumptions, target market selection and customer segmentation, go-to-market pricing, channels and sales launch, IP/technology commercialization, operating model design and capability gap analysis, organization structure and culture change.

experience.description:
Purpose: Helping others see new opportunities and have the courage to pursue them. 

Works with clients to define and operationalize purpose-led strategic roadmaps, innovative new business models, and more effective organizational operating models to realize transformational strategies. 

Current leadership role focused on defining innovative strategies, collaborative business models, viable value-based payment models across the healthcare ecosystem to address health disparities and impact social determinants of health (SDOH). 

Recent state and local government projects include “reimagining the future” of Medicaid, SNAP / Food is Medicine, TANF and WIC, enabling community-based care ecosystems, transforming child and family services, expanding community health worker (CHW) networks, accelerating the transition to home-based care, telehealth and remote care modalities, improving transportation infrastructure, and leveraging technology and leveraging data analytics to demonstrated outcomes.

experience.position: Adjunct Professor of Strategy, Design Thinking, and Business Model Innovation
experience.description: Working with graduate students and startup CEOs to apply design thinking principles and frameworks to identify, test, launch and scale disruptive new business model innovations by working in "real-world" situations. Preparing students to integrate disciplines of business strategy, design thinking, operating model transformation, and change management to accelerate innovation and commercialization.

Led strategy and innovation-related initiatives to refocus CareFusion's product portfolio on cross-business, "horizontal" innovations integrating product, process, platform and data to improve patient safety and reduce preventable harm with clinically-relevant information at the point of care.

CareFusion is a global medical device and technology company solely focused on improving patient safety by combining innovative products. Part of leadership team during the carve-out of CareFusion from its parent Cardinal Health, a Fortune 20  medical products manufacturer and pharmaceutical distributor.

Responsible for cross-BU, "horizontal" innovation culture, capabilities, process, governance and operating model at Cardinal Health. Defined customer-focused strategy and innovation roadmap for Infection Prevention to address unmet needs of surgeons, nurses, infection control and other key hospital stakeholders focused on reducing healthcare-associated infections (HAIs). Led initial feasibility assessment and collaborative partnership discussions, licensing and deal structuring negotiations with multiple biotech and medical device technology vendors to develop and commercialize medical device innovations.

Significant hands-on new venture experience across a variety of B2B and B2C industries.  Strategos is a 25-person innovation consulting boutique founded by Professor Gary Hamel (Core Competence of the Corporation, HBR, 1990) and a small group of experienced strategy consultants and former corporate executives. Strategos works collaboratively with its clients to develop game-changing strategies and commercialize new-to-the-world product ideas and business model concepts while building the culture, skills and infrastructure for on-going innovation inside the client organization.

Founding Member of Ernst & Young’s Strategic Advisory Services (SAS) practice that grew from a core group of 5 to 150+ strategists and ~$25M in two years.  Significant firm-building, methodology development and project sales and delivery leadership roles.  

NOTE:  In May 2000, Cap Gemini acquired Ernst & Young Consulting and its Strategic Advisory Services (SAS) practice.

about:
Seasoned, results-driven advisor focused on driving growth, innovation, and profitability for clients in manufacturing sectors including chemicals, materials, and industrial products.

My consulting experience is comprised of engagements on a variety of functional topics, with focus on driving the performance and growth of organizations. Recent work has included corporate/business unit strategy, operating model design, pre- and post-deal transaction support, and R&D transformation. With the rapid advancement of AI and related technologies, I am particularly interested in helping companies fundamentally reinvent and transform how their value chains operate

Prior to my consulting career, I have nearly 10 years of industry experience as a researcher, product developer, and project leader focused on commercialization, process improvement, and plant support. I began my career in GE’s Edison Engineering Development Program, during and after which I assumed an active leadership role on several cross-functional and global projects in chemicals and advanced materials.

Lastly and most importantly, I help individuals grow in their careers through formal performance management and informal mentorship. I enjoy reflecting on my varied experiences to help people figure out "what they want to be when they grow up," contemplate a career switch if needed, and succeed in consulting or industry - while reserving the right to be authentic.

All views my own.

publications.title: Why Should the World Invest in Women
publications.description:
Women have been subjugated since long, as far as one can remember, and often, men have been the perpetrators of this subjugation. Our society harbors a deep imbalance when it comes to gender parity, and this has led to horrendous social, psychological, and economic deficiencies, across sectors. But, with the rise of the new social generation and a renewed information age, the case for supporting women has been strong. 

I co-authored the book, Why Should the World Invest in Women attempts to strengthen this thought by way of interaction. We interacted with corporate titans, prominent film producers, civil leaders, public servants, young change-makers and seasoned development professionals to decode the case of investment in women, why it is the need of the hour and how all of us can become an active part of it.

about:
I help B2B leaders turn underperforming partnerships into engines of strategic growth.

For over three decades, I’ve led and advised growth initiatives across the full business lifecycle from startups to Fortune 100 companies. My work spans telecom, SaaS, AI, and digital infrastructure, with more than $3B in partnership-driven revenue across the U.S., Asia, and Europe.

I’m the author of Unlocking Strategic Growth: The Mindset Behind Business Development Success, a practical guide now used by business leaders and teams to sharpen execution, expand market reach, and strengthen alliance strategy.

I work with:
• Global B2B enterprises
• PE-backed and expansion-stage companies
• Founders and GTM leaders looking to accelerate through partnerships

What I bring:
• Pattern recognition from three decades of cross-border execution
• Strategic clarity on what derails partnerships and how to fix it
• A proven ability to turn strategy into measurable revenue

Notable results:
• $702M in contribution margin through partner-led growth
• Scaled revenue from $30M to $3B in APAC within five years
• Strategic advisory across U.S. entry, M&A-linked partnerships, and cross-regional BD

If you’re a CEO, CRO, or investor-backed founder and need a strategic advisor or interim executive to help drive revenue, stabilize key partnerships, or expand internationally, I’m open to the right engagements.

receivedRecommendations.givenByHeadline: Chief Customer Officer / Strategic Advisor
receivedRecommendations.givenAt: August 14, 2013, Hastings reported directly to Gregory
receivedRecommendations.description:
Greg Wade built and then led the BlackBerry business in Southeast Asia for around 6 years. When Greg arrived in the region the company was firmly focused on business segment customers and was a small part of the BlackBerry's total business. Greg led the thinking around and execution of BlackBerry's hugely successful move into consumer segments in Southeast Asia from 2008-9. This idea was to prove to be extremely successful for BlackBerry, delivering high single digit billion USD incremental revenue to BlackBerry between 2009-12, culminating in Southeast Asia moving from around 6% to 17% of company annual revenue in only 4 years. 

This provided a clear long term example of Greg being able to think in a structured way, understand the opportunities to leverage and the problems to overcome, and to design an organizational architecture that will execute effectively. 

It was under this initiative that Greg hired me into BlackBerry. I was hired by Greg to create and execute the move into consumer distribution channels in the region. Greg showed his ability to think outside of the box - I was an unorthodox hire, was new to the region, but provided new insight into consumer segments that Greg was looking for. Greg has the ability to think 'around corners' - discerning patterns and trends, articulating solutions for them early. 

Greg was a popular leader - due to the fact he was genuine, effective and empathetic. He has a rare combination of possessing strong EQ whilst being a straight shooter. Greg would always provide the unvarnished truth alongside encouragement to his teams to determine and execute the most effective business strategy, regardless of whether it was in line with BlackBerry's traditional direction or not. By 2011-12 employee engagement scores from Greg's team of ~150FTE were some of the highest within BlackBerry. 

As a direct manager, one of Greg's strengths was his genuine motivation to develop his team. He was an ardent supporter of personal and career development and his ideas in this area were company leading. Greg was an effective mentor, with the ability to understand where he could learn through 'doing', leveraging his perspective and skill-set. 

Partners respected and trusted Greg - he formed long term C level relationships with channel partners, carriers and customers, He is an active participant in adjacent external organizations with consistent volunteer service to regional Chambers of Commerce.

Performance outcomes for BlackBerry in Southeast Asia under Greg's management were clearly superior - however while his team will acknowledge the significant growth they delivered, I think they will more likely remember that Greg simply created a good place to work - people understood the regional vision and what was expected from them, were given the trust and resources to think and execute well, in return good things happened both for them personally and for the company, and importantly, they had fun.

I graduated from the University of Southern California with an undergraduate degree in Architecture, minors in Business and Real Estate Development, and a graduate degree in finance from the Marshall School of Business. about:
Most of us take the built environment for granted. We rely on transit systems, highway networks and utility grids to travel anywhere and achieve anything, yet rarely consider how the necessary infrastructure arrived and how it remains functional. At the nexus of project finance and client advisory, I work with policymakers, stakeholders, and decision makers to advance all components of infrastructure development, making life as we know it possible.

As an analyst for EY Infrastructure Advisory, I have worked on wide-ranging transportation and infra projects for clients nationwide, including intercity rail, broadband, private and public transit-oriented development, and statewide transportation prioritization.

profileTopEducation.schoolName: Cornell University

experience.description:
Perform financial analysis of major capital infrastructure projects for clients in all sectors, including creating comprehensive financial models and reports, developing presentations for client executives and industry leadership, and coordinating project schedules and procurements.
Projects/clients include: intercity passenger rail financial feasibility study, transportation funding report for an east coast state DOT, revenue generation for an east coast city transit agency, southeast state turnpike authority, TOD for a west coast transit agency, TOD and RRIF loan application for a large western city, grant advisory for rural broadband delivery, and on-site hotel development at a southern state fairgrounds.

Provided a major American transit agency with recommendations to enhance revenues through value capture techniques, passenger fares flexibility, and COVID-related special federal grants, as well as evaluated the strategies deployed by peer transit agencies nationwide to offset pandemic-driven ridership losses without permanently reducing service.
Evaluated the credentials of potential lessees as part of a procurement for a first-of-its-kind offshore wind development on the East Coast.
Researched the successes and failures of several mid-size American cities in their respective light rail developments to compile a system expansion plan for an established, and growing, light rail operator.

projects.description: Project developed during the Infrastructure Finance course taken during my final Cornell semester in which I evaluated the financial feasibility of a Chicago Transit Authority (CTA) system expansion along the city's peripheral Western Avenue corridor. Report included key assumptions, ridership projections, cash flows and flows of funds, sources and uses (including TIFIA and TIFIA 49 loans), debt amortization, and analysis of risks. publications.title: What Though P-values Conspire to Cheat You: Save Your Greatest Failure
publications.description:
Whenever we conduct a quantitative study (usually based upon logical positivism), we instinctively look for ‘statistically significant’ p-values, defined as those that are less than .05 or .01. At the very moment when we confront non-significant p-values, many of us tend to fidget and declare the study a failure, although we know that the cut-off value of p (alpha level) is arbitrary at best. Some scientists simply shelve the data and move on to the next project without sharing what they've learned.

This editorial discusses the publication bias phenomena and initiates discussions on the importance of addressing it.

publications.title: Six Sigma Project Tracking Software Review
publications.description:
Despite the uniqueness of the Six Sigma programs that are being implemented worldwide, there are many common measures by which all of these programs gauge their success – the alignment of projects to business strategy, utilization of Belts, project completion, best-practice sharing and achieved financial benefits, to name a few.

What is common across these metrics is the ability to track projects and monitor project performance. Some companies choose to craft an in-house solution for tracking Six Sigma projects. Another option that appeals to many organizations is an offthe- shelf, customizable software program to manage all the data associated with project tracking.

These project tracking programs can perform a multitude of functions, from monitoring project deliverables to reporting collectively on project status enterprise wide, from facilitating knowledge sharing through a project database to tracking financial metrics. The programs are used by virtually anyone involved in a Six Sigma deployment – executives, Six Sigma Champions and deployment leaders, Master Black Belts, project leaders, and team members.

For this article, four of the most popular Six Sigma project tracking software programs were reviewed: EnterpriseTrack 4.3 from Instantis, i-Nexus 3.1, PowerSteering 5.0 and SixNet 2.9.

All four of these programs have proven track records in the industry, and each has its own strengths and unique features that set it apart from the others. This article may help you decide which one could be right for your organization.

publications.title: When and How to Adopt Zero-Based Budgeting
publications.publishedAt: EPM and Business Intelligence Executive Insight · Oct 1, 2014
publications.description:
Zero-based budgeting can be an effective tool to reset the budget and planning process. While not for every
company or every situation, when there is significant change, a high level of cost pressure, or the cost structure has
become stale, ZBB helps target improvement by focusing on true cost drivers. Companies have seen sustainable
cost improvements of 25% or more by adopting this budget method. These organizations train employees to treat
every dollar of expense as if it were their own, instilling financial discipline in the organization and operating in an
environment where cost management is a way of life

publications.title: Large Global Diversified Company Retools FP&A
publications.description:
The subject of this case study is a large global manufacturer with a significant presence in numerous industries.
Over time, the company evolved and expanded both through acquisitions and organic growth. This led to the
adoption of a decentralized management approach to its hundreds of operating companies in dozens of countries.
While advantageous in many respects, this model increased the finance organization’s operating costs, particularly
in providing FP&A services. To address the issue, finance embarked on a planning-process transformation initiative
designed to improve efficiency and reduce cost while boosting service levels. Within the first year of the initiative,
over 60% of internal survey respondents rated the target-setting process as “better” or “significantly better” than in
prior years. Further, some business units successfully adopted the best practice of linked planning events, saving major
amounts of time and eliminating unnecessary work

publications.title: Obtaining Structure-Borne Input Power for a SEA Model of an Earthmoving Machine Cab
publications.publishedAt: SAE 2011 Noise and Vibration Conference and Exhibition · May 6, 2011
publications.description: Properly characterizing input forces is an important part of simulating structure-borne noise problems. The purpose of this work was to apply a known force reconstruction technique to an earthmoving machinery cab to obtain input functions for modeling purposes. The technique was performed on a cab under controlled laboratory conditions to gain confidence in the method prior to use on actual machines. Forces were measured directly using force transducers and compared to results from the force reconstruction technique. The measured forces and vibrations were used as input power to an SEA model with favorable results.

publications.title: Vibro-acoustic model of an enclosed electric power generator
publications.publishedAt: Journal of the Acoustical Society of America (2010) · Apr 14, 2010
publications.description: A vibro-acoustic model of an enclosed diesel-powered electric generator was built using commercial vibro-acoustics software (primarily SEA) and empirical methods. The vibro-acoustic sources, including the engine, generator, cooling fan, and exhaust were characterized experimentally for several different operating conditions. The vibro-acoustic performance of the enclosure and sound suppression features were modeled and experimentally validated. Good agreement was achieved between experimental and simulated results.

about:
Jared is an Associate Director with EY-Parthenon Global Talent in London, United Kingdom and has his MBA from the Kellogg School of Management, Northwestern University. Every day, he wakes up with a passion to explore the world such that he can impact, educate and lift up those around him. This reigns true as his purpose in reaffirming a commitment to discover our uniqueness, venture to branch out and leverage inclusion for growth.

Jared was previously employed as an Assistant Director in Diversity, Equity & Inclusiveness with EY, and prior to that, as a Senior Consultant, Global Treasury Services with EY. He has held roles with Exelon, Allegion, PNC Financial Services, BlueCross BlueShield and Morgan Stanley Smith Barney. 

Jared championed work and dialogue around promoting Diversity & Inclusion while at Kellogg through serving as President for the Kellogg Evening & Weekend Pride at Kellogg organization and work as an Admissions Ambassador with specific attention to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion. He has previously served as lead over the Exelon Diversity & Inclusion Partnership Program, a vast supplier diversity program. Jared has also previously served as a board member on the Auxiliary Board of Northwestern Memorial.

Jared completed his undergraduate education at Loyola University Chicago and earned his Bachelor of Business Administration in Economics/Finance. He also studied abroad in Rome, Italy at the John Felice Rome Center. 

When not in the office, you can find him planning his next mountain to summit, heading to Heathrow for a weekend trip or training on the Thames Path for his next marathon. 

Specialties: Diversity Program Development, Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Strategy, Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Consulting, Supplier Diversity Program Development, Culture and Belonging Facilitation

honorsAndAwards.description:
Innovative idea award on CHESSBOARD, a strategic scenario modelling decision making tool. In a typical organization, senior executives often needs to make decision in a short period of time. CHESSBOARD provides a platform to formulate strategic options and evaluates multiple scenarios in a structured manner enabling sound decision making. It can synchronize data with internet of things and provide cost-benefit insights of the options. 

In addition, it can simulate scenarios with an array of parameters to evaluate risk and cost in order to proactively plan for the next steps. With a solid database of industry benchmark, executives can run different options and compare cost and benefits. Examples of parameters could be shift timeline due to regulatory filings, currency fluctuations, interest rates increase, commodity seasonality cycle and real estate volatility.

volunteering.description:
I serve on the Housing and Facilities Committee of the Board of Directors of Sarah's Circle. I support the organization, leveraging my experience in real estate, public policy, and planning, in its critical push to providing more interim and permanent supportive housing for homeless women in Chicago.

Sarah’s Circle is a refuge for women who are homeless or in need of a safe space. By providing housing assistance, case management, referral services, and life necessities, we encourage women to empower themselves by rebuilding both emotionally and physically; realizing their unique potential.

We have a 50-bed interim housing program, which is the largest program of this type in the City; daytime support center for those who are street homeless, doubled-up with friends or family, or at risk of homelessness; and 30 units of permanent supportive housing for the most vulnerable. Women in these programs access case management and clinical services to help them move quickly into permanent homes and deal with core issues that contributed to their homelessness in the first place. Women who become housed are able to stay engaged through the Daytime Center to insure long term housing stability.

publications.title: Rethinking Airport Parking Facilities to Protect and Enhance Non-Aeronautical Revenue
publications.publishedAt: Airport Cooperative Research Program (ACRP) Sponsored by the Federal Aviation Administration · Mar 4, 2021
publications.description:
Ongoing and emerging shifts in customer ground access behavior, resulting from the growing use of transportation network companies (TNCs) and the eventual adoption of emerging technologies, are posing a significant challenge to the reliance of airports on parking revenue.

The TRB Airport Cooperative Research Program's ACRP Research Report 225: Rethinking Airport Parking Facilities to Protect and Enhance Non-Aeronautical Revenues is a guidance document that identifies near-term and long-term solutions to help airports of all types and sizes repurpose, renovate, or redevelop their parking facilities to address the loss of revenue from airport parking and other ground transportation services.

headline: M&A Strategy | Ernst & Young, Ex A&M, Deloitte, KPMG, Recipient of 4 Gold Medals - MBA Finance, BIMTECH
about:
As a Mergers and Acquisitions Senior Associate at Alvarez & Marsal, I apply my expertise in all phases of the M&A process to deliver successful outcomes for clients. I have a proven track record of leading and executing complex transactions, conducting financial and operational due diligence, and providing strategic advice.

I have a strong academic background in finance, having graduated from BIRLA INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT TECHNOLOGY (BIMTECH) with a PGDM-International Business (Finance) degree, where I was a gold medalist and a recipient of multiple scholarships. I also cleared CFA Level 1 in 2018, demonstrating my knowledge and skills in financial analysis and risk management.

Prior to joining Alvarez & Marsal, I worked as a solution advisor for M&A strategy at Deloitte, where I drafted diligence reports, performed advanced analyses on over 30 deals, and led the consumer sector team for the Chicago region. I also mentored two new joiners and increased the team integration by 12%. Before that, I worked as a solution advisor for M&A at Deloitte, where I was involved in six end-to-end M&A transactions.

I am passionate about the M&A industry and constantly seek to learn and grow. As a managing director in the Transactions and Corporate Finance practice, Christine guides real estate investors and funds on the design, implementation and operation of their valuation process and strategy. Christine has extensive experience project management, preparation of valuation opinions and valuation reviews for all purposes (tax, financial reporting, etc.), real estate asset diligence, scenario modeling, real estate portfolio optimization, strategy and valuation process improvement. Utilizing her real estate sector experience, she supports organizations through transactions and transformations.

Christine earned a BBA in Real Estate and Urban Land Economics from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Christine received the counselor of real estate (CRE) designation in 2021.

How Christine is building a better working world . . .
I’m always thinking about how I can be a better connector. There is nothing I enjoy more than facilitating meaningful interactions between our clients and EY professionals to not only enhance productivity, but to drive innovation and growth.

headline: Partner/Principal at EY-Parthenon | Answering strategic questions in software and professional services sectors
about:
Ben Kadish is a management consultant serving private equity sponsors, and executives of public and privately held corporations.

He has more than 20 years of experience in the software economy across various strategy consulting and corporate functional roles. 

Ben leads the legal technology subsector and co-leads the professional services subsector for EY-Parthenon’s Private Equity business. In software, he has deep experience across a wide range of legal tech and professional services tech subsectors, and significant depth in non-profit, integrated payments, and eCommerce software, among other subsectors. In professional services, Ben is a leader in advising on the accounting, office of the CFO, and legal services sectors. 

Ben has deep experience in private equity and M&A transactions, having supported more than 150 deals.  A proven problem solver and thought leader, Ben's insights and perspectives have been published in business media targeting the CEO, corporate strategy groups, and investors.

During his consulting career, Ben's key strategic experience has included advising private equity sponsors, the C-suite, corporate development, and corporate strategy clients on strategic M&A, market entry, competitive strategy, growth strategy, due diligence, and go-to-market strategy.

Shekar has managed a wide variety of projects including process improvement, distribution center operations design, warehouse management system implementation, operational readiness testing, supply chain network strategy, capacity analysis, and go-live support.

Some of his past clients include:
•    The US's largest beauty products retailer
•    The US's largest automotive products retailer
•    Art & craft products retailer
•    Industrial automation equipment provider
•    Boeing research & technology
 
Prior to taking up a career in management consulting, Shekar focused on building a strong technical foundation by completing master’s degree programs in Supply Chain and Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech where he was a graduate researcher. 

Shekar lives in Chicago, IL and when not working, he likes to travel, explore new neighborhoods and restaurants, learn music, and participate in the local general aviation community.

My expertise spans end-to-end portfolio oversight, including transaction management, lease administration, workplace strategy, organizational redesign, process improvement and leveraging outsourced partnerships to drive operational efficiency and cost savings while aligning real estate with broader corporate goals.

A key strength is advising clients through complex mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures, where I manage the full lifecycle of real estate portfolio transitions. This includes site separation and integration planning, workplace planning and occupancy optimization, redesign of the corporate real estate function and operating model, implementation of supporting technologies, refinement of internal processes, and coordination of outsourced providers to minimize disruption, capture synergies, and position the portfolio for long-term success. 

My passion is partnering with executives to transform corporate real estate into a strategic asset that supports business growth, enhances employee experience, and delivers measurable financial and operational value

headline: Consulting Associate @ EYP/Owner at Sunrise Topiaries
about:
Founding businesses and helping them grow has always been my passion. I've always enjoyed the small things, starting from nothing and slowly watching plans take shape in front of me. Through hard work, dedication, and out-of-the-box thinking, I have always loved to change the world, even if only in my own small way.

I currently consult businesses big and small using my past expertise. In my own career, working in various internships, leading my own small business, and now as a strategy consultant, I have worked in many different fields - from M&A to retail. I've had experience working with suppliers, governments and working on back-end technological platforms. I've also had experience in sales, interacting with customers and working to meet the needs of my clients however and wherever possible.

Over the past few years I have had the opportunity to work as an intern at both small startups all the way to fortune 500 businesses. I hope to take my own experiences in entrepreneurship, coupled with my time in strategy consulting, to own my own outcomes an strategies at a business in the future. What sets me apart as an individual is my out of the box thinking, and my ability to take the initiative no matter what situation I am placed in.

headline: Partner at EY-Parthenon | Working Capital | AI adoption in real operations
about:
As a partner with EY-Parthenon, I have experience serving several multinational clients and PE-backed companies. I support executive leadership in developing and implementing practical strategies to liberate cash flow from working capital.  

I believe the best strategies are the ones that work in the real world. My focus is helping businesses unlock cash that is tied up in everyday processes, so they can reinvest in growth and resilience. Today, that includes using AI in practical ways to transform processes, accelerate decision-making, and reduce friction across the value chain.

I'm also hugely passionate about increasing collaboration and inclusion in our working world.

headline: Markets ∙ Innovation ∙ Sustainability
about:
Calvin Chu Yee Ming is Partner at EY-Parthenon. He has advised senior executives in over 20 countries, including organizations such as 3M; ADB, AIA; Bell Labs; Canon; Coca-Cola; Cummins; DBS; DHL; Disney; Fujitsu; HP; Intel; General Electric; M1; MasterCard; Medtronic; Nikkei; Nokia; Reed Elsevier; Roche; Samsung; SKF; StarHub; Standard Chartered Bank; Sumitomo; TNT; UNDP; UNESCO; UNICEF; and VISA; as well as the governments of Australia; Denmark; Indonesia; Korea; Malaysia; New Zealand; Philippines; Singapore; and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

Calvin was recognised as a NetImpact Change-maker in 2014 and inducted into the International Who’s Who of Professionals in 2009. His work has appeared in Asian Banking & Finance, Asia Pacific Biotech News, BusinessWeek, The Star, the Straits Times, the Singapore Business Review, Today, and the Wall Street Journal, and he has featured at the ASEAN Smart Cities Network, ASEAN Social Entrepreneurship Forum, The Economist Social Innovation in Action, the Regional CEO & CIO Summit, Asia-Pacific CFO Summit, Business & Nature Forum, Institutional Investors APAC Summit, Singapore Business Federation, TEDx, Education Innovation, Prepaid Mobile Asia, Private Healthcare Asia, and Biomedical Business Conference.

Calvin has been a Judge, Reviewer, and Mentor at the President's Challenge Social Enterprise Award, The Grand Challenges Explorations (GCE) Program of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, MIT Inclusive Innovation Challenge, MIT Emerging Technologies Innovators Under 35, the Youth Social Enterprise Programme Grant Committee, The DBS-NUS Social Venture Challenge Asia, The Grameen Creative Lab, the Lee Kuan Yew Global Business Plan Competition, Social Innovation Camp Asia, Start-up@Singapore, and The University of Chicago Booth School of Business Global New Venture Challenge. He has also served as an iAdvisor with IE Singapore, an Executive Advisor at NUS Enterprise, and on the boards of BioFourmis, Bettr Lives, Conjunct Consulting, New Energy Nexus Ventures, Rotary Club, and the World Toilet Organization.

The views expressed on this account represent Calvin’s personal opinions and do not necessarily represent the position of EY.

experience.description: EY-Parthenon brings a unique combination of transformative strategy, transactions, tax and corporate finance to design, develop, and deliver practical, end-to-end solutions. My team and I focus on social innovation, economic growth and development, helping clients manage complexity to achieve measurable and sustainable outcomes.

Eden Strategy Institute was an impact consulting practice focusing on Social Innovation and Sustainability, that has helped multinational organizations, governments, and development agencies achieve sustainable economic, environmental, and social advantage, by designing and introducing new growth platforms, operations, products, and services. We specialized in social innovation, systems thinking, capability building, corporate social partnerships, inclusive business models, sustainable finance, and impact assessment. Our work transformed developmental gaps into market opportunities in smart cities, value-based healthcare, education innovation, public service transformation, and the emerging middle class. The company was recognized as The Most Innovative Management Consultancy in APAC Insider’s Singapore Business Awards; Corporate Livewire’s Management Consultancy of the Year; Global 100’s Most Innovative Management Consultancy (Singapore); Corporate Vision’s Best Social Innovation Consultancy (Singapore); and was also the winner of the National Business Award in the Consulting category by the Singapore Business Review. In 2025, the practice of Eden Strategy Institute was acquired to be part of EY-Parthenon, where our team continues to focus on social innovation, economic growth and development.
Lecturer on Strategic Management & Organisational Theory to final-year business undergraduates

Singapore Exchange Limited (SGX) is Asia-Pacific's first demutualised and integrated securities and derivatives exchange. Home to Singapore's listed companies, SGX is at the forefront of exchanges globally in attracting international issuers and is rapidly emerging as Asia's offshore risk management centre for international derivatives. The Business & Strategy Development unit identifies, evaluates, plans, and implements innovative business models, partnerships, products, and platforms to realise new growth opportunities for the exchange.

Synovate Business Consulting (now Ipsos Business Consulting) is a global, London-listed firm that supports Fortune 500 companies in their strategic decisions, delivering research-based market insights, innovative value propositions and business models, as well as practical implementation plans across industries and countries.

As one of the ten largest market intelligence firms in the world, Synovate's specialties include feasibility planning; risk assessment; market sizing, segmentation, and entry; partner evaluation; scenario planning and wargaming; corporate intelligence; business branding; value chain analysis; innovation consulting and value proposition development; competitive, marketing, and growth strategy

publications.description: How employees are on-boarded and welcomed into their new positions sets the tone for the culture of a place, the people, and the values of a new institution and can have a significant impact on employees sense of belonging. At Ohio University, the Division of Student Affairs employs approximately 400 staff and annually welcomes around 40-50 new employees a year, 25 of which are College Student Personnel (CSP) graduate students. New employees are welcomed with an ethic of care through a five day onboarding process rooted in Bolman and Deal’s human resource frame. This process includes departmental specific welcomes and trainings, along with division-wide team building, sexual misconduct training, social justice training, and suicide prevention training. This session outlined the correlation with Bolman and Deal’s human resource frame and NASPA/ ACPA competencies as well as lessons learned from implementing such a process, specifically include how these trainings intersect with the learning and development of new professionals.

publications.publishedAt: Proceedings of The 5th China International Conference on Insurance and Risk Management (CICIRM 2014) · Jul 23, 2014
publications.description: Based on theoretical analysis of the pricing model and the pension model with houses at home and abroad, the paper focus on analyzing and measuring three risk factors of reverse mortgage pricing including life expectancy, housing price fluctuations and loan interest rate. Combining with the risks it faced, we establish pricing models of lump-sum payment, annuity payment and annuity payment with increasing benefits. The actual data is collected to prove the Pension Model with Houses after formula derivation. The paper put forward policy proposals of implementation together with feasibility analysis .

publications.description:
The Litigation Services Handbook is the definitive guide for financial experts engaged in litigation services. Attorneys require financial experts now more than ever, and this book provides the guidance you need to provide a high level of service as witness and consultant. Enhance your litigation skills as you delve into the fine points of trial preparation, deposition, and testimony; project authority under examination, and hold up to tough questions under cross-examination. Fraud investigations are a major component of litigation support services, and this book delves deep into Sarbanes-Oxley compliance and other relevant topics to give you a foundational understanding of how these cases are prosecuted, and your role as the financial services expert. This updated sixth edition includes new coverage of technology's role in the financial expert's practice, and the focus on investigations provides practical insight from leading experts in the field. From the process itself to proving damages, this indispensable reference covers all aspects of litigation services. 
Providing litigation support requires more than just your financial expertise; you also need a working knowledge of relevant case law, and a deep understanding of both the litigation process and the finer points of courtroom appearances. This book provides the insight and perspective you need to provide superior service to attorneys and their clients. 
•	Understand your role in trial preparation and testimony presentation
•	Provide authoritative responses to direct and cross examination
•	Examine and analyze Sarbanes-Oxley rulings
•	Lend financial expertise to fraud investigations
The growing demand for financial expert litigation services has created a niche market for CPAs, creating a lucrative opportunity for qualified accountants who also possess the specialized knowledge the role requires. The Litigation Services Handbook is THE essential guide for anyone involved in financial litigation.

volunteering.description:
The Civic Leadership Foundation (CLF) prepares underserved teenagers for college, career and active citizenship.  CLF partners with principals, teachers, and youth program directors to deliver empowering, project-based curriculum that teaches young people critical life-long leadership skills such as collaboration, resourcefulness and accountability.

The core of every CLF program is Civic Leadership Education - a comprehensive, project-based program designed to empower young people toward a deeper sense of responsibility for self and to community, preparing them for college, career and civic life. 

Civic Leadership Education focuses on three broad categories of skills: collaboration, resourcefulness and accountability.  Each phase of the program provides an opportunity for youth to think, act and reflect on those skills through systematic lesson plans that encourage young people to learn and practice those capabilities they will need to be successful, engaged adults.  Through readings, discussions, reflective activities and self-directed projects, young people take on increasingly responsible leadership roles that culminate in Civic Leadership Projects in which the youth identify a community concern, and then plan, execute and evaluate a project to address that concern.  CLF’s programs seek to develop and nurture a growing sense of agency among participants and to connect them constructively to their community.

Civic Leadership Education programs can be adapted to various lengths (from 40 hours to multi-year) and are currently in use in public and charter schools, afterschool programs, juvenile justice facilities and community-based social service organizations throughout Chicago and beyond. 

In addition, CLF programs are combined with internships, job placements, and integrated with other activities to accomplish the following goals:

Career and Job Readiness 
Violence Prevention and Mitigation 
Service Learning and Civic Readiness
School Readiness

headline: Director at EY-Parthenon
about:
As a Director at EY-Parthenon’s Transaction Strategy and Execution practice, I lead and execute complex transactions, integrations, and turnarounds, ensuring value creation for our clients, primarily within the Life Sciences sector.

I am responsible for leading workstreams, translating client needs into actionable tasks and deliverables, and managing day-to-day problem-solving and team analytics. I serve as a key liaison between our consulting team, Senior Directors and Partners at EY-Parthenon, and client leadership. Through this, I ensure cohesive collaboration and alignment on strategic objectives, guiding clients through high-impact mergers, spin-offs, and divestitures.

Recently, I spearheaded the integration of two $500M medical aesthetics companies, realizing $70M in recurring cost savings through synergy management and operational alignment. I’ve also led Post-Close PMO teams for a $75B Life Sciences corporation and developed comprehensive models to mitigate stranded costs from spin-offs. My experience extends to managing TSAs across 62+ countries and working with cross-functional teams on a global scale.

Prior to EY, I spent 5 years in the Heavy Construction sector, leading teams in project planning, supply chain management, and engineering functions across a variety of commercial and industrial structures.

With an MBA from The University of Chicago Booth School of Business, I focused on strategic management, finance, and entrepreneurship, which deepened my passion for M&A strategy, improving financial performance, and market expansion.

I am always looking for opportunities to drive growth and transformation, whether within consulting or in-house strategy roles, where my experience in complex transactions and integration leadership can contribute to success.

publications.title: Her Demands
publications.description:
Home to the indigenous Purépecha people, Cherán is historically known to be one of the most violent
municipalities in the state of Michoacán, México. The Purépecha have suffered from acute crimes, including rape, kidnappings, murder, and environmental destruction of their forests as a result of the Mexican government colluding with illegal loggers. In 2011, an uprising led by a group of women banned police, politicians, and any form of the Mexican government from their village. Since then, the village has successfully governed its own people and achieved autonomy, leading to a drastic decrease in crime and restoration of their invaluable forests. The present narrative is a rendition of the actual events that happened in Cherán right before the uprising from the perspective of a 12-year-old girl as she witnesses environmental destruction in her community. The characters in the narrative are fictional. Cherán’s history shows that communal effort results in the community’s prosperity.

headline: Senior Director, Corporate Finance | EY-Parthenon
about:
Kevin serves as a senior director at EY Parthenon and has been delivering valuation and corporate finance services for over 9 years.

He graduated in 2016 with a Bachelor of Science in Business Administration, specializing in finance, from the Fisher College of Business at The Ohio State University. During his time at Ohio State, Kevin was an active member of the Fisher Futures investment banking organization and also earned a minor in engineering sciences. He broadened his horizons by studying abroad for a semester at Audencia Nantes Ecole de Management, a prestigious business school in Nantes, France.

Kevin began his professional journey in 2016 with the business valuation team at Ernst & Young, where he played a key role in engagements related to businesses, business interests, and intangible assets for both public and private companies. In 2020, he transitioned to the business valuation group at Citizens Bank to gain fresh insights into the valuation industry, before returning to Ernst & Young's corporate finance team in 2022. Since rejoining the EY strategy and transactions group (now known as EY-Parthenon), Kevin has established himself as a leading technical valuation expert within the national practice and has successfully managed a transformative strategy-based project for a Fortune 500 client.

Kevin has held the Chartered Financial Analyst designation since 2019.

Outside of work, Kevin enjoys golfing, traveling, cheering for Cleveland and Ohio State sports teams, and spending quality time with friends and family.

headline: Valuation Solutions - Senior Director at EY-Parthenon
about:
Jim Arvin is a Senior Director in EYP's Corporate Finance Valuation Solutions practice specializing in the valuation of capital equipment. Since joining in 2010, Jim has accumulated extensive experience in conducting and overseeing valuations for various purposes. These include federal tax planning, purchase price allocations, state property taxes, impairment testing, and embedded intangible studies. Jim's expertise extends across multiple industries—power & utilities, retail, healthcare, pharmaceutical, defense, and telecommunications—and spans the US as well as international markets.

Jim was selected as a plan fellow of World Business Chicago from September 2015 through January 2016. As a plan fellow, he contributed to the development of a strategic framework for the Metro Chicago Exports (MCE) initiative, which can be found under strategy five in former Mayor Emanuel’s 2012 Plan for Economic Growth and Jobs.

publications.title: Englewood Black-Owned Small Businesses: Documenting Effects of COVID-19 and the Black Lives Matter Movement of 2020
publications.description: Media accounts report that the COVID-19 pandemic and 2020 Black Lives Matter (BLM) movement disproportionately affected Black communities and businesses, amplifying existing racial health and economic disparities. Research literature is now striving to provide analyses of Black business owners’ experiences in 2020. The present research uses mixed methods to discern the impacts of 2020 crises on small businesses in Englewood, Chicago. The study examined Chicago-area foot traffic data from SafeGraph cell-phone records to identify business visitation patterns relative to two events: the March 21 Illinois stay-at-home order and the commencement of BLM protests after the murder of George Floyd on May 25. After both March 21 and May 25, there were statistically significant changes in foot traffic in majority-Black neighborhoods as compared to majority-non-Black neighborhoods. The research further elucidated the complexity of the mechanisms by which COVID-19 and BLM activities disproportionately influenced Black communities through semi-structured interviews with Black-identifying small business owners (n=8) in Englewood. Qualitative NVivo analyses detailed participants’ evolving perceptions of policing in Englewood after looting in June, concern for employee well-being in the pandemic, and complex grant application processes throughout 2020. After the initial evaluations and findings, the study employed NVivo to map relationships among the significant foot traffic patterns and participants’ lived experiences, specifically examining business owners’ reactions to the March 21 and May 25 events. This project provides insight into the range of experiences Black entrepreneurs in Englewood faced in 2020 and suggests ways that policy responses might usefully support their survival and success.

I graduated summa cum laude from Miami University's Farmer School of Business with a Master of Accountancy and Bachelor of Science in Business with an Accountancy major and Information Security minor. I hold alumni status with Beta Gamma Sigma and Beta Alpha Psi.

I am passionate about technology and innovation, especially in how the ways in which we work, interact, and strategize are influenced by available technologies. I have experience with creating tools to assist my teams in Alteryx, Power BI, and Tableau; creating and debugging basic programs in Python, Java, and JavaScript; and working with major ERP systems and databases.

headline: Director at EY-Parthenon | Supply Chain & M&A Operations Leader
about:
I am a strategic operations leader with experience across the M&A lifecycle, in both divestitures and acquisitions. My career is rooted in the mechanics of the legal system, and complimented by an MBA focused on Accounting and Finance. I have become a trusted partner to to senior executives within Fortune 50 companies, using rigorous analytical skill coupled with deal experience to help organizations navigate ambiguous situations and complex changes. 

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗜 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴: 
•	Deal Management: Facilitated five separations and integrations over the past five years, directing teams of up to 35 to support various deal stages from signing through post close and Transition Services exits. 

•	C-Suite Communication: Refine complex analyses into concise messaging, regularly presenting deal progress, risks, and synergy or stranded cost implications to senior level deal management and C-suite level executives. 

•	Cost Management and Strategic Execution: Trusted to help both PE and strategic buyers minimize stranded costs and margin decreases through thorough diligence review and strategic sourcing. 

•	Foundations in Deal Mechanics and Analytical Rigor: Former attorney with deal training in both a law school and MBA environment, with the ability to take large quantities of qualitative and quantitative information and distill actionable insights. 

•	Team Leadership: Regularly manage teams spanning multiple continents, and proven track record of successfully driving results and developing high performing teams.

I have built a reputation for keeping teams focused on long term growth and results during uncertain circumstances and providing the insights needed to align stakeholders on a path forward during complex decision making. I am focused on growing my impact in the transaction space as I continue to build my leadership skills and drive value within growing organizations.

experience.description:
M&A Integration & Procurement Operations: Led end-to-end integration of IT procurement systems, processes, and organizational structures during $5B aerospace and defense merger from signing through close, conducting contract due diligence, synergy capture analysis, value realization planning, and cross-functional coordination to deliver Day 1 operational readiness and seamless procurement transition.

Transaction Risk Mitigation: Directed contract analysis and supply chain continuity planning for $2.5B medical device spinoff, reviewing direct supply agreements for all product lines, coordinating with category management, RemainCo and SpinCo legal teams, and developing risk mitigation strategies to preserve supplier relationships and minimize leverage loss.

Post-close Transaction Services and Cost Optimization: Managed TSA exits and contract separation for $26B healthcare technology spinoff. Coordinated RemainCo and SpinCo dependencies, IT infrastructure changes, minimizing stranded cost exposure, and executing strategic sourcing initiatives that delivered $18.5M in cost avoidance for SpinCo operations.

Global Strategic Sourcing: Established enterprise global mobility program for $35B healthcare technology company. Managed operations, billing, and sourcing across 40+ countries, coordinating cross-functional global stakeholders, and implementing contract infrastructure valued at $240M annually to support international workforce.

Transaction Execution and Supply Chain Operations: Carve-out execution for $30B Advanced Manufacturing divestiture, coordinating legal entity separation, regulatory compliance, contract disentanglement, and operational transition planning to achieve Day 1 readiness for global warehouse logistics and supply chain operations.

Transaction Planning and Hypercare Management: Organizational separation for $2B manufacturing spinoff from $20B parent, developing standalone and run rate cost structures, workforce transition planning, TSA scoping, vendor and customer contract and PO cutover, and multi-continental change management programs to establish independent operational infrastructure.

Technology sales and implementation: Partnered with C-suite executives at top 100 global law firms to negotiate and renew enterprise agreements worth up to $3m annually. Supported technology integration into law firm operations and managed training programs and educational material development.  

Strategic Account Management: Conducted client consultations, competitive analyses, and industry benchmarking to deliver tailored AI and legal technology solutions that supported firm objectives and operational efficiency. Consistently achieved 98% or more of sales targets across all markets.

Regulatory Compliance: Managed portfolio of approximately 100 telecommunications infrastructure projects at a time for major carriers (AT&T and Verizon). This included reviewing lease agreements, property records, chain of title documentation, federal regulatory standards (FCC/FAA), and construction blueprints to ensure site compliance.

Contract Management & Negotiation: Managed leases and project timelines for each site while renegotiating residential and commercial landlord agreements across approximately 100 concurrent site upgrades, achieving up to $200k in cost savings per site.

Operational Assessment and Improvement: Collaborated with hospital teams to analyze and optimize billing operations, collection workflows, and process inefficiencies through Epic Hospital Billing Application implementation, delivering strategic solutions that improved cash flow and reduced collection cycle time by 25%.
